text:
nina: quick follow-up from yesterday's RFC thread. I sketched a concrete scoring approach for windowed demotion + fragmentation accounting. want to validate assumptions before I turn it into an addendum.

sam: sounds good. high-level question: are we optimizing for small-allocation microbatch workloads first? that influences window size.

nina: yes — goal is microbatch=1-8 common paths. short-lived host-backed pages are the main churners. we saw ~70% < 200ms in a recent sample.

taylor: reminder: time-windowed scoring helps reduce random thrash vs pure LRU but we must be careful with prefetch interplay. async prefetches could rehydrate pages we just demoted.

maria: what about making window adaptive to observed sequence length per-tenant? e.g., window_ms = base * mean_seq_len_factor. simple flag to enable.

jordan: makes sense. also we should penalize evicting slabs that fragment badly. small free holes are expensive on VRAM. current metric: slab_hole_bytes / slab_total_bytes.

nina: proposal (pseudo):

score = hotness_score(window_ms, recency_weight) - frag_penalty(frag_ratio, slab_size) + prefetch_confidence_bonus

where frag_penalty = frag_ratio * frag_weight * log(1 + slab_size_kb)

Notes: hotness_score in [0..100], prefetch_confidence_bonus in [0..20] when prediction high.

sam: implementation concerns: global sorting of candidates is costly. use coarse buckets: cold (0-33), warm (34-66), hot (67-100). eviction normally picks from cold; when pressure high, scan warm bucket with lightweight sampling.

taylor: agree. maintain O(1) amortized insertion into buckets. only do an O(k log k) sort when bucket hits a pressure threshold.

maria: ops: PCIe/swap link saturation is real. ops-bot telemetry shows sustained bursts up to 85% during training spikes. we must back off demotes when link_util > 75%.

ops-bot: pci_tx_util 6155556400..6155556750 avg 58%, 95th 84%. demote_rate correlated with spikes.

jordan: policy idea: when pci_util > 75% -> increase window_ms by factor 1.5 and require higher prefetch confidence to demote. also prefer batched async demotes to avoid small frequent transfers.

nina: tests: add a deterministic repro in eng-runtime/tests/demotion_repro.py that allocs million tiny tensors, staggered lifetimes, and records demote/prefetch counts + pci bytes.

sam: telemetry plan: expose histograms per-tenant: hotness_bucket_count, frag_ratio_p95, demote_ops/sec, pci_tx_bytes/sec, prefetch_mispred_rate. dashboard + alert if latency p50 regresses > 25ms during canary.

taylor: rollout plan: feature-flag gated -> canary on pool-4 -> compare ingress latency and pci util. auto-disable if tail lat > baseline_tail + 30ms for 5m.

maria: one more fairness question: charge fragmentation to tenant? i.e., when reclaiming a slab with many holes, attribute the fragmentation penalty to last-owner so multi-tenant fairness preserved. cost accounting event emitted on reclaim.

jordan: prefer last-owner amortization; fallback is split-charge by allocation count when last-owner unknown. document in RFC addendum.

nina: ok next steps I will: 1) draft RFC addendum (scoring formula, bucket design, canary plan), 2) patch offload controller to read slab frag metadata, 3) add pci util soft-signal, 4) add tests + telemetry. aiming for PoC in 2 sprints.

sam: thanks, file ENG-RUNTIME-1428 has been created: https://redwood.internal/issue/ENG-RUNTIME-1428

ops-bot: deploy-preview: offload-controller/feature/windowed-demote enabled on canary-pool-4 at 6155556803

taylor: I'll take the PoC allocator changes. maria pls own telemetry fields. jordan can you write the last-owner heuristics notes?

maria: on it.

jordan: will do.

nina: great. tagging folks to coauthor: @taylor @maria @jordan. I'll send a PR for the addendum by EOD.
